Approximate broadcasting of quantum correlations

Wei Xie1 Email: xievvvei@gmail.com Affiliation: 1Centre for Quantum Software and Information, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Technology Sydney, NSW 2007, Australia    Kun Fang1 Email: kun.fang-1@student.uts.edu.au Affiliation: 1Centre for Quantum Software and Information, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Technology Sydney, NSW 2007, Australia    Xin Wang1 Email: xin.wang-8@student.uts.edu.au Affiliation: 1Centre for Quantum Software and Information, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Technology Sydney, NSW 2007, Australia    Runyao Duan1,2 Email: runyao.duan@uts.edu.au Affiliation: 1Centre for Quantum Software and Information, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Technology Sydney, NSW 2007, Australia Affiliation: 2UTS-AMSS Joint Research Laboratory for Quantum Computation and Quantum Information Processing, Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100190, China
August 24, 2026
Abstract

Broadcasting quantum and classical information is a basic task in quantum information processing, and is also a useful model in the study of quantum correlations including quantum discord. We establish a full operational characterization of two-sided quantum discord in terms of bilocal broadcasting of quantum correlations. Moreover, we show that both the optimal fidelity of unilocal broadcasting of the correlations in an arbitrary bipartite quantum state and that of broadcasting an arbitrary set of quantum states can be formulized as semidefinite programs (SDPs), which are efficiently computable. We also analyze some properties of these SDPs and evaluate the broadcasting fidelities for some cases of interest.

I Introduction

Copying information is a rather simple task in the classical realm, but unfortunately not in the quantum realm. It is not allowed to create an identical copy of an arbitrary unknown pure quantum state due to the no-cloning theorem [1, 2]. One can clone a set of pure states if and only if they are orthogonal. The no-broadcasting theorem [3] generalizes this result to mixed states, saying that a set of quantum states can be broadcast if and only if the states commute with each other.

These no-go theorems can be further extended to the setting of local broadcast for composite quantum systems. Given a bipartite quantum state ρA​B\rho_{AB} shared by Alice and Bob, their objective is to perform local operations only (without communication) to produce a state ρ^A1​A2​B1​B2=(ΛA→A1​A2⊗ΓB→B1​B2)​ρA​B\widehat{\rho}_{A_{1}A_{2}B_{1}B_{2}}=(\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}A_{2}}\otimes\Gamma_{B\to B_{1}B_{2}})\rho_{AB} such that TrA1​B1⁡ρ^A1​A2​B1​B2=TrA2​B2⁡ρ^A1​A2​B1​B2=ρA​B\operatorname{Tr}_{A_{1}B_{1}}\widehat{\rho}_{A_{1}A_{2}B_{1}B_{2}}=\operatorname{Tr}_{A_{2}B_{2}}\widehat{\rho}_{A_{1}A_{2}B_{1}B_{2}}=\rho_{AB} (see Section II for notational convention). It is shown in [4] that this task can only be performed if ρA​B\rho_{AB} is classically correlated. Even if the task is relaxed to obtain two bipartite states with the same correlation as ρA​B\rho_{AB} (measured by the mutual information), it is feasible to do the task if and only if the given state ρA​B\rho_{AB} is classically correlated. This is called the no-local-broadcasting theorem [4]. Furthermore, when the local operations ar only allowed for one party (e.g., Alice), the task can be done if and only if ρA​B\rho_{AB} is classical on AA [5, 6, 7].

When the task of perfect broadcasting cannot be accomplished, it is natural to ask whether the broadcasting can be performed in an approximate fashion, and how to design the optimal broadcasting operation. We shall study the approximate broadcasting of states and correlations by utilizing semidefinite programs (SDPs). In Ref. [8] the Bose-symmetric channel is considered as unilocal broadcasting operation and an SDP is derived for this problem. Semidefinite programming optimization techniques [9] have found many applications to the theory of quantum information and computation (see, e.g., [10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18]), and also to the study of quantum correlations (see, e.g., [19, 20, 8, 21]).

Quantum discord (see Section III for definition), as an indispensable measure of quantum correlation beyond entanglement, is introduced in [22] and [23] independently. It is argued [24] that quantum discord is responsible for the quantum speed-up over classical algorithms. Quantum discord is a quite useful concept in many fields of quantum information processing, such as local broadcasting of correlations [4, 25], quantum computing [26], quantum data hiding [27], quantum data locking [28], entanglement distribution [29, 30], common randomness distillation [31], quantum state merging [32, 33, 34], entanglement distillation [34, 35], superdense coding [34], quantum teleportation [34], quantum metrology [36], and quantum cryptography [37]. Quantum discord has become an active research topic over the past few years [38, 39].

The local broadcasting paradigm can provide a natural operational interpretation to quantum discord. Remarkably, the minimum average loss of mutual information resulting from local operation ΛA→A1⋯An\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}\cdots A_{n}} on AA for arbitrary quantum state ρA​B\rho_{AB} approaches the quantum discord DA​(ρA​B)D_{A}(\rho_{AB}) of ρA​B\rho_{AB} as nn goes to infinity. This result is established in Ref. [25] and it generalizes the work in Ref. [40] which considers pure states ρA​B\rho_{AB} only. However, it remains open whether there is an analogous connection for the two-sided setting of redistributing correlations [39].

In this paper, we study the approximate broadcasting of quantum correlations in both asymptotic and non-asymptotic settings. In the asymptotic regime, we rigorously prove the conjecture in Ref. [39] and show an operational meaning of the two-sided discord in terms of bilocal broadcasting of correlations; that is, the asymptotic minimum average loss of correlation after optimal bilocal broadcasting is exactly the two-sided quantum discord of the initial state. In the non-asymptotic regime, we give an alternate derivation for the SDP characterization of the optimal unilocal broadcasting fidelity and show that the universal quantum clone machine (UQCM) can also serve as the optimal universal unilocal broadcasting operation. Moreover, the optimal state-dependent unilocal broadcasting operation for pure two-qubit states is analytically solved. Similarly, we establish the SDP for the optimal broadcasting fidelity of a finite set of quantum states.

II Preliminaries

A quantum system AA is associated to a Hilbert space ℋA{\cal H}_{A} of dimension |A||A| with some fixed orthonormal basis {|j⟩A}j\{|j\rangle_{A}\}_{j}. In this work, we only deal with finite-dimensional spaces, and the spaces of systems with the same letter are always assumed to be isomorphic, for example, ℋA≅ℋA~≅ℋA1≅ℋA2{\cal H}_{A}\cong{\cal H}_{\widetilde{A}}\cong{\cal H}_{A_{1}}\cong{\cal H}_{A_{2}}. The linear operators from ℋA{\cal H}_{A} to ℋB{\cal H}_{B} are always written with subscripts identifying the systems involved, for example, XA→BX_{A\to B}. We denote 𝒮⁡(A){\cal S}(A) as the set of density operators [41] on system AA.

A quantum operation (or channel) ℰA→B{\cal E}_{A\to B} with input system AA and output system BB is a completely positive (CP), trace preserving (TP) linear map from the linear operators on ℋA{\cal H}_{A} to the linear operators on BB. A quantum-to-classical channel ℱ{\cal F} is a cptp map such that ℱ(⋅)=∑jTr(Mj⋅)|j⟩⟨j|{\cal F}(\cdot)=\sum_{j}\operatorname{Tr}(M_{j}\cdot)|j\rangle\!\langle j|, where {Mj}j\{M_{j}\}_{j} is a POVM. The set of all quantum-to-classical channels is denoted by QC. Since the subsript of an operator or operation specifies its input and output systems, we can write a product of operators or operations without the ⊗\otimes symbol, and omit the identity operator or operation 𝟙{\mathds{1}}, which would make no confusion, for example, XA​B​YB​C≡(XA​B⊗𝟙C)​(𝟙A⊗YB​C)X_{AB}Y_{BC}\equiv(X_{AB}\otimes{\mathds{1}}_{C})({\mathds{1}}_{A}\otimes Y_{BC}) and ℰB→C​(XA​B)≡(𝟙A⊗ℰB→C)​XA​B{\cal E}_{B\to C}(X_{AB})\equiv({\mathds{1}}_{A}\otimes{\cal E}_{B\to C})X_{AB}.

The Choi-Jamiołkowski matrix [42, 43] of a quantum operation ℰA→B{\cal E}_{A\to B} is Jℰ=(𝟙A~→A~⊗ℰA→B)​ϕA~​AJ_{{\cal E}}=({\mathds{1}}_{\widetilde{A}\to\widetilde{A}}\otimes{\cal E}_{A\to B})\phi_{\widetilde{A}A}, where ϕA~​A=∑i​j|i​i⟩​⟨j​j|\phi_{\widetilde{A}A}=\sum_{ij}|ii\rangle\!\langle jj| is the unnormalized maximally entangled state. The output of the channel ℰA→B{\cal E}_{A\to B} with input ρA\rho_{A} can be recovered from JℰJ_{{\cal E}} by ℰA→B​(ρA)=TrA⁡(JℰTA​ρA){\cal E}_{A\to B}(\rho_{A})=\operatorname{Tr}_{A}(J_{{\cal E}}^{T_{A}}\rho_{A}), where TAT_{A} denotes the partial transpose on AA.

We use H⁡(⋅)H(\cdot) to denote the von Neumann entropy of quantum states, H⁡(A|B):=H⁡(A​B)−H⁡(B)H(A|B)\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=H(AB)-H(B) the conditional quantum entropy, I⁡(A:B):=H⁡(A)+H⁡(B)−H⁡(A​B)I(A\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B)\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=H(A)+H(B)-H(AB) the quantum mutual information. The fidelity F⁡(ρ,σ)=Tr⁡ρ​σ​ρF(\rho,\sigma)=\operatorname{Tr}\sqrt{\sqrt{\rho}\sigma\sqrt{\rho}}, as a measure of similarity between quantum states, can be viewed as the optimal solution to an SDP [44, 45]. The diamond norm can be used to give the distance of two quantum operations ℰ,ℱ{\cal E},{\cal F}, that is, ∥ℰ−ℱ∥⋄=sup{∥((ℰ−ℱ)⊗𝟙)X∥1:∥X∥1=1}\|{\cal E}-{\cal F}\|_{\diamond}=\sup\{\|(({\cal E}-{\cal F})\otimes{\mathds{1}})X\|_{1}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}\|X\|_{1}=1\}, where ∥⋅∥1\|\cdot\|_{1} is the trace norm. In addition, we denote [n]={1,…,n}[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}, and denote by |⋅||\cdot| the cardinality of a set or the dimension of a linear space.

III Asymptotic bilocal broadcasting and two-sided quantum discord

III.1 Previous results

The concept of quantum discord was introduced by [22, 23]. Here the one-sided and two-sided quantum discord of a bipartite state ρA​B\rho_{AB} are defined by

DA​(ρA​B):=minℰA∈QC⁡(I​(A:B)ρA​B−I​(A:B)(ℰA⊗𝟙B)​ρA​B),D_{A}(\rho_{AB})\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\min_{{\cal E}_{A}\in\text{QC}}(I(A\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B)_{\rho_{AB}}-I(A\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B)_{({\cal E}_{A}\otimes{\mathds{1}}_{B})\rho_{AB}}), (1)
DA​B​(ρA​B):=minℰA,ℱB∈QC⁡(I​(A:B)ρA​B−I​(A:B)(ℰA⊗ℱB)​ρA​B),D_{AB}(\rho_{AB})\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\min_{{\cal E}_{A},{\cal F}_{B}\in\text{QC}}(I(A\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B)_{\rho_{AB}}-I(A\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B)_{({\cal E}_{A}\otimes{\cal F}_{B})\rho_{AB}}), (2)

respectively.

It is shown in [25] that the one-sided quantum discord is equal to the asymptotic average loss of correlation after the optimal broadcasting operation. Consider the following scenario. Alice and Bob, apart away from each other, share a bipartite quantum state ρA​B\rho_{AB}. The information, or correlation, shared by them is measured by quantum mutual information in what follows. The goal of Alice is to broadcast the mutual information between them to many, say nn, recipients, using local operation only. If the state is not classical on AA, she cannot perform the task perfectly [5, 6, 7], and the mutual information between each recipient and Bob would decrease in general. Now her task naturally becomes to design a broadcasting operation in order to minimize the average loss of mutual information. Remarkably, the minimal average loss of correlation approaches quantum discord DAD_{A} of ρA​B\rho_{AB} as nn tends to infinity, as revealed in the following Proposition.

Proposition 1 ([25])

Let ρA​B\rho_{AB} be a bipartite state and DAD_{A} is defined by Eq. (1). Let ΛA→A1​…​An\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}\dots A_{n}} be a cptp map and Λj:=Tr\Aj∘Λ\Lambda_{j}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{j}}\circ\Lambda. Then

DA​(ρA​B)=limn→∞minΛA→A1​…​An⁡1n​∑j=1n(I​(A:B)ρA​B−I​(Aj:B)(Λj⊗𝟙B)​ρA​B).\begin{split}&D_{A}(\rho_{AB})\\ =&\lim_{n\to\infty}\min_{\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}\dots A_{n}}}\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\left(I(A\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B)_{\rho_{AB}}-I(A_{j}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}B)_{(\Lambda_{j}\otimes{\mathds{1}}_{B})\rho_{AB}}\right).\end{split}

IV Optimal universal and state-dependent broadcasting of correlations

We now turn to the non-asymptotic regime of the local broadcasting of quantum correlations. We first study the optimal universal unilocal broadcasting and then the optimal state-dependent unilocal broadcasting.

IV.1 Optimal universal unilocal broadcasting

We first give a general definition for the unilocal nn-broadcasting fidelity of a bipartite state.

Definition 4

Given a bipartite state ρA​B\rho_{AB}, the optimal unilocal nn-broadcasting fidelity of ρA​B\rho_{AB} on system AA (see Fig. 1) is defined as the following optimal fidelity

fn(ρA​B)=sup{1n​∑j=1nF⁡(ρA​B,Tr\Aj​B⁡ΛA→A1​…​An​(ρA​B)):ΛA→A1⋯An is a quantum channel}.\begin{split}f_{n}(\rho_{AB})=\sup\Bigl\{&\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}F(\rho_{AB},\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{j}B}\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}...A_{n}}(\rho_{AB}))\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}\\ &\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}\cdots A_{n}}\text{ is a quantum channel}\bigl\}.\end{split} (9)

Since the set of quantum channels is compact and the fidelity function is continuous [50], the supremum in Eq. (9) is attained. Define a unitary operator WπW_{\pi} on systems A1⋯AnA_{1}\cdots A_{n} for each permutation π∈Sn\pi\in S_{n}, by the action

Wπ|j1,j2,…,jn⟩=|jπ−1​(1),jπ−1​(2),…,jπ−1​(n)⟩W_{\pi}|j_{1},j_{2},\dots,j_{n}\rangle=|j_{\pi^{-1}(1)},j_{\pi^{-1}(2)},\dots,j_{\pi^{-1}(n)}\rangle

for any choice of |j1⟩,|j2⟩,…,|jn⟩|j_{1}\rangle,|j_{2}\rangle,\dots,|j_{n}\rangle. A quantum channel ΛA→A1⋯An\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}\cdots A_{n}} is called a symmetric broadcasting channel, if

Λ⁡(ρ)=Wπ​(Λ⁡(ρ))​Wπ†\Lambda(\rho)=W_{\pi}(\Lambda(\rho))W_{\pi}^{\dagger}

for any ρ∈𝒮⁡(A)\rho\in{\cal S}(A) and π∈Sn\pi\in S_{n}.

We notice that for any channel ΛA→A1⋯An\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}\cdots A_{n}} and π∈Sn\pi\in S_{n}, Λ⁡(⋅)\Lambda(\cdot) and Wπ​(Λ⁡(⋅))​Wπ†W_{\pi}(\Lambda(\cdot))W_{\pi}^{\dagger} give the same average fidelity in Eq. (9), since

Tr\Aj​B⁡ΛA→A1​…​An​(ρA​B)\displaystyle\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{j}B}\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}...A_{n}}(\rho_{AB})
=\displaystyle= Tr\Aπ−1​(j)​B⁡Wπ​(ΛA→A1​…​An​(ρA​B))​Wπ†.\displaystyle\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{\pi^{-1}(j)}B}W_{\pi}(\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}...A_{n}}(\rho_{AB}))W_{\pi}^{\dagger}.

Thus 1n!​∑π∈SnWπ​(Λ⁡(⋅))​Wπ†\frac{1}{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_{n}}W_{\pi}(\Lambda(\cdot))W_{\pi}^{\dagger}, which is a symmetric broadcasting channel, also gives the same value. So we only need to consider the supremum over symmetric broadcasting channels. In Eq. (9), when Λ\Lambda is a symmetric broadcasting channel, the summands are all the same.

Therefore, the optimal unilocal nn-broadcasting fidelity of a bipartite state ρA​B\rho_{AB} on AA can be rewritten as

fn​(ρA​B)=max{F(ρA​B,Tr\A1​BΛA→A1​…​An(ρA​B)):ΛA→A1⋯An is a symmetric broadcasting channel}.\begin{split}f_{n}(\rho_{AB})=&\max\{F(\rho_{AB},\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{1}B}\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}...A_{n}}(\rho_{AB}))\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}\\ &\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}\cdots A_{n}}\text{ is a symmetric broadcasting channel}\}.\end{split} (10)

It is verified that ΛA→A1⋯An\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}\cdots A_{n}} is a symmetric broadcasting channel iff its Choi matrix JΛJ_{\Lambda} satisfies JΛ=Wπ​JΛ​Wπ†J_{\Lambda}=W_{\pi}J_{\Lambda}W_{\pi}^{\dagger} for any π\pi, i.e., JΛ=1n!​∑π∈SnWπ​JΛ​Wπ†J_{\Lambda}=\frac{1}{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_{n}}W_{\pi}J_{\Lambda}W_{\pi}^{\dagger}. Using this symmetry, we give the SDP characterization for optimal unilocal broadcasting fidelity as follows.

Theorem 5

The optimal unilocal nn-broadcasting fidelity of ρA​B\rho_{AB} on AA is given by the optimal solution of the following SDP,

fn​(ρA​B)=max12​Tr⁡(XA​B+XA​B†)s.t.(ρA​BXA​BXA​B†Tr\A1​B⁡(JTA​ρA​B))≥0,JAA1⋯An≥0,Tr\AJAA1⋯An=𝟙A,JAA1⋯An=1n!∑π∈SnWπJAA1⋯AnWπ†,\displaystyle\begin{split}f_{n}(\rho_{AB})=\max&\ \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{Tr}(X_{AB}+X_{AB}^{\dagger})\\ \mathrm{s.t.}&\ \begin{pmatrix}\rho_{AB}&X_{AB}\\ X_{AB}^{{\dagger}}&\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{1}B}(J^{T_{A}}\rho_{AB})\end{pmatrix}\geq 0,\\ &\ J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}\geq 0,\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A}J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}={\mathds{1}}_{A},\\ &\ J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}=\frac{1}{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_{n}}W_{\pi}J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}W_{\pi}^{\dagger},\end{split} (11)

where WπW_{\pi} acts on A1⋯AnA_{1}\cdots A_{n}.

Proof.

It suffices to consider the symmetric broadcasting channels only. Let JAA1⋯AnJ_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}} be the Choi matrix of ΛA→A1⋯An\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}\cdots A_{n}}, then for any ρA\rho_{A},

ΛA→A1⋯An(ρA)=TrA(JAA1⋯AnTAρA).\displaystyle\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}\cdots A_{n}}(\rho_{A})=\operatorname{Tr}_{A}(J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}^{T_{A}}\rho_{A}).

By linearity, for any ρA​B\rho_{AB},

(ΛA→A1⋯An⊗𝟙B)ρA​B=TrA(JAA1⋯AnTAρA​B),\displaystyle(\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}\cdots A_{n}}\otimes{\mathds{1}}_{B})\rho_{AB}=\operatorname{Tr}_{A}(J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}^{T_{A}}\rho_{AB}),

and

Tr\Aj​B(Λ⊗𝟙B)ρA​B=Tr\Aj​B(JAA1⋯AnTAρA​B).\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{j}B}(\Lambda\otimes{\mathds{1}}_{B})\rho_{AB}=\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{j}B}(J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}^{T_{A}}\rho_{AB}).

Now we can rewrite the optimization problem in Eq. (10) in terms of the Choi matrix of Λ\Lambda as

fn​(ρA​B)=maxF⁡(ρA​B,ρ^A​B)s.t.ρ^A​B=Tr\A1​B(JAA1⋯AnTAρA​B),JAA1⋯An≥0,Tr\AJAA1⋯An=𝟙A,JAA1⋯An=1n!∑π∈SnWπJAA1⋯AnWπ†.\displaystyle\begin{split}f_{n}(\rho_{AB})=\max&\ F(\rho_{AB},\widehat{\rho}_{AB})\\ \mathrm{s.t.}&\ \widehat{\rho}_{AB}=\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{1}B}(J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}^{T_{A}}\rho_{AB}),\\ &\ J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}\geq 0,\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A}J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}={\mathds{1}}_{A},\\ &\ J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}=\frac{1}{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_{n}}W_{\pi}J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}W_{\pi}^{\dagger}.\end{split} (12)

The fidelity function F⁡(ρ,σ)F(\rho,\sigma) of two states ρ,σ\rho,\sigma is given by the optimal solution of the following SDP [44, 45],

F⁡(ρ,σ)=max12​Tr⁡(X+X†)s.t.(ρXX†σ)≥0.\displaystyle\begin{split}F(\rho,\sigma)=\max&\ \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{Tr}(X+X^{\dagger})\\ \mathrm{s.t.}&\ \begin{pmatrix}\rho&X\\ X^{{\dagger}}&\sigma\end{pmatrix}\geq 0.\end{split} (13)

Combining Eqs. (12) and (13) gives the desired SDP (11).   ⊓\sqcap⊔\sqcup

Remark  The only difference between the SDP (11) and that in Ref. [8] lies in the symmetry of the broadcasting channel, that is, J=Wπ​J​Wπ†J=W_{\pi}JW_{\pi}^{\dagger} for any π∈Sn\pi\in S_{n} is required in our SDP. In Ref. [8], it is required that J=Wπ1​J​Wπ2†J=W_{\pi_{1}}JW_{\pi_{2}}^{\dagger} for any π1,π2∈Sn\pi_{1},\pi_{2}\in S_{n} which makes sure that the output state lies in the symmetric subspace. These two SDPs are different generalization of perfect unilocal broadcasting. But the SDP (11) here has a more direct derivation, and it is clear that the optimal solution to SDP (11) is no less than that to the SDP in [8]. Numerical experiments show that the two SDPs give the same optimal solution for some cases of ρA​B\rho_{AB}, but we do not know how to give a rigorous proof or disproof for general case up to now.

In the SDP (11), if (JAA1⋯An,XA​B)(J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}},X_{AB}) is feasible solution of f⁡(ρA​B)f(\rho_{AB}), then ((𝟙A⊗U⊗n)JAA1⋯An(𝟙A⊗U⊗n)†,(UA⊗VB)XA​B(UA⊗VB)†)(({\mathds{1}}_{A}\otimes U^{\otimes n})J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}({\mathds{1}}_{A}\otimes U^{\otimes n})^{\dagger},(U_{A}\otimes V_{B})X_{AB}(U_{A}\otimes V_{B})^{\dagger}) is feasible solution of f⁡((UA⊗VB)​ρA​B​(UA⊗VB)†)f((U_{A}\otimes V_{B})\rho_{AB}(U_{A}\otimes V_{B})^{\dagger}) for any local local unitaries UAU_{A} and VBV_{B}. In other words, the unilocal broadcasting fidelity fnf_{n} is invariant under local unitaries.

We now consider the unilocal broadcasting fidelity of a pure state ψA​B:=|ψ⟩​⟨ψ|A​B\psi_{AB}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=|\psi\rangle\!\langle\psi|_{AB}, and especially the maximally entangled state, under the action of the symmetric broadcasting channel. The optimal unilocal broadcasting fidelity fnf_{n} of a pure state ψA​B\psi_{AB} can be written as

fn​(ψA​B)=maxTr⁡(ρ^A​B​ψA​B)s.t.ρ^A​B=Tr\A1​B(JAA1⋯AnTAψA​B),JAA1⋯An≥0,Tr\AJAA1⋯An=𝟙A,JAA1⋯An=1n!∑π∈SnWπJAA1⋯AnWπ†,\displaystyle\begin{split}f_{n}(\psi_{AB})=\max&\ \sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}(\widehat{\rho}_{AB}\psi_{AB})}\\ \mathrm{s.t.}&\ \widehat{\rho}_{AB}=\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{1}B}(J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}^{T_{A}}\psi_{AB}),\\ &\ J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}\geq 0,\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A}J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}={\mathds{1}}_{A},\\ &\ J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}=\frac{1}{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_{n}}W_{\pi}J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}W_{\pi}^{\dagger},\end{split} (14)

where WπW_{\pi} acts on A1⋯AnA_{1}\cdots A_{n}.

The corresponding dual SDP is

fn​(ψA​B)=minTr⁡YAs.t.YA,ZAA1⋯An Hermitian,TrB⁡(ψA​BTA​ψA1​B)−YA+Z−1n!​∑π∈SnWπ†​Z​Wπ≤0,\displaystyle\begin{split}f_{n}(\psi_{AB})=\min&\ \sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}Y_{A}}\\ \mathrm{s.t.}&\ Y_{A},Z_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}\text{ Hermitian},\\ &\ \operatorname{Tr}_{B}\left(\psi_{AB}^{T_{A}}\psi_{A_{1}B}\right)-Y_{A}\\ &\ +Z-\frac{1}{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_{n}}W_{\pi}^{\dagger}ZW_{\pi}\leq 0,\end{split} (15)

where, again, WπW_{\pi} acts on A1⋯AnA_{1}\cdots A_{n}.

It is verified that the strong duality holds by Slater’s theorem since JAA1⋯An=𝟙/|A|nJ_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}={\mathds{1}}/|A|^{n} is in the relative interior of the feasible region of SDP (14). That means the optimal solutions to SDPs (14) and (15) concide.

Proposition 6

The optimal unilocal 2-broadcasting fidelity of the maximally entangled state Φd:=|Φd⟩​⟨Φd|\Phi_{d}\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=|\Phi_{d}\rangle\!\langle\Phi_{d}| with |Φd⟩=1d​∑j=0d−1|j​j⟩|\Phi_{d}\rangle=\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}|jj\rangle on systems A​BAB is given by

f2​(Φd)=d+12​d.f_{2}(\Phi_{d})=\sqrt{\frac{d+1}{2d}}.
Proof.

We prove this proposition by explicitly constructing feasible solutions in primal and dual problem both of which can achieve the value of d+12​d\sqrt{\frac{d+1}{2d}}.

In the primal problem, we take

JA​A1​A2=∑i=0d−1|vi⟩​⟨vi|,J_{AA_{1}A_{2}}=\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}|v_{i}\rangle\langle v_{i}|, (16)

where

|vi⟩=12​(d+1)​(2​|i⟩⊗|i​i⟩+∑j≠i|j⟩⊗(|i​j⟩+|j​i⟩))|v_{i}\rangle=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2(d+1)}}(2|i\rangle\otimes|ii\rangle+\sum_{j\neq i}|j\rangle\otimes(|ij\rangle+|ji\rangle))

This operation is also known as the universal quantum copying machine (UQCM) [51, 52].

In the dual problem, we take

YA=d+12​d2𝟙d,ZA​A1​A2=−d+1d3(dΦd−I0)⊗𝟙d,Y_{A}=\frac{d+1}{2d^{2}}{\mathds{1}}_{d},\ Z_{AA_{1}A_{2}}=-\frac{d+1}{d^{3}}(d\Phi_{d}-I_{0})\otimes{\mathds{1}}_{d},

where I0=∑i=0d−1|i​i⟩​⟨i​i|I_{0}=\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}|ii\rangle\langle ii|.   ⊓\sqcap⊔\sqcup

Remark  It is interesting that the optimal unilocal 2-broadcasting channel of the maximally entangled state is the same as the UQCM which comes from the global broadcasting setting. There is much progress on quantum cloning machine that has been made in the past years (see, e.g., [53, 54]). For d⊗dd\otimes d bipartite maximally entangled state, its optimal unilocal 2-broadcasting channel is denoted as ΥA→A1​A2d\Upsilon_{A\rightarrow A_{1}A_{2}}^{d} with Choi matrix (16) and

TrA2⁡ΥA→A1​A2d​(ρA)=d+22​d+2​ρA+12​d+2​𝟙d,\operatorname{Tr}_{A_{2}}\Upsilon_{A\rightarrow A_{1}A_{2}}^{d}(\rho_{A})=\frac{d+2}{2d+2}\rho_{A}+\frac{1}{2d+2}{\mathds{1}}_{d},

is a depolarizing channel.

Next, we will introduce a worst-case quantifier for the performance of unilocal broadcasting of a symmetric channel.

Definition 7

For any symmetric broadcasting channel ΛA→A1⋯An\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}\cdots A_{n}}, we define the unilocal broadcasting power 𝒫⁡(Λ){\cal P}(\Lambda) of Λ\Lambda as

𝒫⁡(Λ):=infρA​B∈𝒮⁡(A​B)F⁡(ρA​B,Tr\A1​B⁡Λ⁡(ρA​B)){\cal P}(\Lambda)\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\inf_{\rho_{AB}\in{\cal S}(AB)}F(\rho_{AB},\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{1}B}\Lambda(\rho_{AB})) (17)

The unilocal broadcasting power of a symmetric broadcasting channel gives a measure of the universal unilocal broadcasting ability for symmetric broadcasting channels. The universality means it is independent of the input state. The channel with a larger value of unilocal broadcasting power is more capable of unilocal broadcasting quantum states in a universal sense.

Based on the result of optimal unilocal 2-broadcasting fidelity of maximally entangled state, we will prove that the optimal unilocal 2-broadcasting channel ΥA→A1​A2d\Upsilon_{A\to A_{1}A_{2}}^{d} for the maximally entangled state has the greatest power for unilocal 2-broadcasting.

Lemma 8

For any d⊗dd\otimes d pure state |ψ⟩|\psi\rangle,

f2​(|ψ⟩​⟨ψ|)≥F⁡(|ψ⟩​⟨ψ|,TrA2⁡ΥA→A1​A2d​(|ψ⟩​⟨ψ|))≥d+12​d.f_{2}(|\psi\rangle\!\langle\psi|)\geq F(|\psi\rangle\!\langle\psi|,\operatorname{Tr}_{A_{2}}\Upsilon_{A\to A_{1}A_{2}}^{d}(|\psi\rangle\!\langle\psi|))\geq\sqrt{\frac{d+1}{2d}}. (18)
Proof.

Consider the Schmidt decomposation |ψ⟩=∑iλi​|i⟩A​|i⟩B|\psi\rangle=\sum_{i}\lambda_{i}|i\rangle_{A}|i\rangle_{B}, where {|i⟩A}i\{|i\rangle_{A}\}_{i} and {|i⟩B}i\{|i\rangle_{B}\}_{i} are some orthonormal bases. Thus,

ρo​u​t=TrA2⁡ΥA→A1​A2d​(|ψ⟩​⟨ψ|)=∑i​jλi​λj​|i⟩​⟨j|⊗(d+22​d+2​|i⟩​⟨j|+12​d+2​𝟙d)=d+22​d+2​|ψ⟩​⟨ψ|+∑i​jλi​λj2​d+2​|i⟩​⟨j|⊗𝟙d.\begin{split}\rho_{out}&=\operatorname{Tr}_{A_{2}}\Upsilon_{A\to A_{1}A_{2}}^{d}(|\psi\rangle\!\langle\psi|)\\ &=\sum_{ij}\lambda_{i}\lambda_{j}|i\rangle\!\langle j|\otimes(\frac{d+2}{2d+2}|i\rangle\!\langle j|+\frac{1}{2d+2}{\mathds{1}}_{d})\\ &=\frac{d+2}{2d+2}|\psi\rangle\!\langle\psi|+\sum_{ij}\frac{\lambda_{i}\lambda_{j}}{2d+2}|i\rangle\!\langle j|\otimes{\mathds{1}}_{d}.\end{split} (19)

Then the second inequality in Eq. (18) follows from

F2​(|ψ⟩​⟨ψ|,ρo​u​t)=F2​(|ψ⟩​⟨ψ|,d+22​d+2​|ψ⟩​⟨ψ|+∑i​jλi​λj2​d+2​|i⟩​⟨j|⊗𝟙d)=d+22​d+2+∑i​jλi​λj2​d+2​⟨ψ|(|i⟩​⟨j|⊗𝟙d)|ψ⟩=d+22​d+2+∑id​λi4(2​d+2)​d≥d+22​d+2+(∑iλi2)2(2​d+2)​d=d+12​d.\begin{split}&F^{2}(|\psi\rangle\!\langle\psi|,\rho_{out})\\ =&F^{2}\left(|\psi\rangle\!\langle\psi|,\frac{d+2}{2d+2}|\psi\rangle\!\langle\psi|+\sum_{ij}\frac{\lambda_{i}\lambda_{j}}{2d+2}|i\rangle\!\langle j|\otimes{\mathds{1}}_{d}\right)\\ =&\frac{d+2}{2d+2}+\sum_{ij}\frac{\lambda_{i}\lambda_{j}}{2d+2}\langle\psi|(|i\rangle\!\langle j|\otimes{\mathds{1}}_{d})|\psi\rangle\\ =&\frac{d+2}{2d+2}+\frac{\sum_{i}d\lambda_{i}^{4}}{(2d+2)d}\\ \geq&\frac{d+2}{2d+2}+\frac{(\sum_{i}\lambda_{i}^{2})^{2}}{(2d+2)d}=\frac{d+1}{2d}.\end{split} (20)

⊓\sqcap⊔\sqcup

Proposition 9

For any d⊗dd\otimes d mixed state ρ\rho,

f2​(ρ)≥F⁡(ρ,TrA2⁡ΥA→A1​A2d​(ρ))≥d+12​d.f_{2}(\rho)\geq F(\rho,\operatorname{Tr}_{A_{2}}\Upsilon_{A\to{A_{1}A_{2}}}^{d}(\rho))\geq\sqrt{\frac{d+1}{2d}}.
Proof.

Suppose ρ=∑jpj​|ψj⟩​⟨ψj|\rho=\sum_{j}p_{j}|\psi_{j}\rangle\!\langle\psi_{j}| is a pure state decomposition of ρ\rho and ρ^j=TrA2⁡ΥA→A1​A2d​(|ψj⟩​⟨ψj|)\hat{\rho}_{j}=\operatorname{Tr}_{A_{2}}\Upsilon_{A\to{A_{1}A_{2}}}^{d}(|\psi_{j}\rangle\!\langle\psi_{j}|), then we have

TrA2⁡ΥA→A1​A2d​(ρ)=TrA2⁡ΥA→A1​A2d​(∑jpj​|ψj⟩​⟨ψj|)=∑jpj​TrA2​ΥA→A1​A2d​(|ψj⟩​⟨ψj|)=∑jpj​ρ^j\begin{split}\operatorname{Tr}_{A_{2}}\Upsilon_{A\to A_{1}A_{2}}^{d}(\rho)=&\operatorname{Tr}_{A_{2}}\Upsilon_{A\to A_{1}A_{2}}^{d}(\sum_{j}p_{j}|\psi_{j}\rangle\!\langle\psi_{j}|)\\ =&\sum_{j}p_{j}\operatorname{Tr}_{A_{2}}\Upsilon_{A\to A_{1}A_{2}}^{d}(|\psi_{j}\rangle\!\langle\psi_{j}|)\\ =&\sum_{j}p_{j}\hat{\rho}_{j}\end{split} (21)

Employing the joint concavity of fidelity, we have that

F⁡(ρ,TrA2⁡ΥA→A1​A2d​(ρ))=F⁡(∑jpj​|ψj⟩​⟨ψj|,∑jpj​ρ^j)≥∑jpj​F​(|ψj⟩​⟨ψj|,ρ^j)≥∑jpj​d+12​d=d+12​d,\begin{split}F(\rho,\operatorname{Tr}_{A_{2}}\Upsilon_{A\to A_{1}A_{2}}^{d}(\rho))=&F(\sum_{j}p_{j}|\psi_{j}\rangle\!\langle\psi_{j}|,\sum_{j}p_{j}\hat{\rho}_{j})\\ \geq&\sum_{j}p_{j}F(|\psi_{j}\rangle\!\langle\psi_{j}|,\hat{\rho}_{j})\\ \geq&\sum_{j}p_{j}\sqrt{\frac{d+1}{2d}}=\sqrt{\frac{d+1}{2d}},\end{split} (22)

where the last inequality uses the result in Lemma 8.   ⊓\sqcap⊔\sqcup

Theorem 10

ΥA→A1​A2d\Upsilon_{A\to{A_{1}A_{2}}}^{d} has the strongest power for unilocal 2-broadcasting in d⊗dd\otimes d system, i.e.,

maxΛ⁡𝒫⁡(Λ)=𝒫⁡(ΥA→A1​A2d),\max_{\Lambda}{\cal P}(\Lambda)={\cal P}(\Upsilon_{A\to{A_{1}A_{2}}}^{d}),

where the maximum is taken over all symmetric broadcasting channels.

Proof.

For any symmetric broadcasting channel ΛA→A1​A2\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}A_{2}}, we have

𝒫⁡(Λ)=infρA​B∈𝒮⁡(A​B)F⁡(ρA​B,Tr\A1​B⁡Λ⁡(ρA​B))≤F⁡(Φd,Tr\A1​B⁡Λ⁡(Φd))≤F⁡(Φd,Tr\A1​B⁡ΥA→A1​A2d​(Φd))=d+12​d,\begin{split}{\cal P}(\Lambda)=&\ \inf_{\rho_{AB}\in{\cal S}(AB)}F(\rho_{AB},\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{1}B}\Lambda(\rho_{AB}))\\ \leq&\ F(\Phi_{d},\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{1}B}\Lambda(\Phi_{d}))\\ \leq&\ F(\Phi_{d},\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{1}B}\Upsilon_{A\to{A_{1}A_{2}}}^{d}(\Phi_{d}))\\ =&\ \sqrt{\frac{d+1}{2d}},\end{split} (23)

where Φd\Phi_{d} is the maximally entangled state. The second inequality holds since ΥA→A1​A2d\Upsilon_{A\to{A_{1}A_{2}}}^{d} is the optimal unilocal 2-broadcasting channel for Φd\Phi_{d}.

For the unilocal 2-broadcasting operation ΥA→A1​A2d\Upsilon_{A\to{A_{1}A_{2}}}^{d}, from Proposition 9, we have that

𝒫⁡(ΥA→A1​A2d)=d+12​d.{\cal P}(\Upsilon_{A\to{A_{1}A_{2}}}^{d})=\sqrt{\frac{d+1}{2d}}. (24)

Combining Eqs. (23) and (24), it is clear that ΥA→A1​A2d\Upsilon_{A\to{A_{1}A_{2}}}^{d} maximizes the unilocal broadcasting power 𝒫{\cal P}. Thus, it is optimal under the setting of universal unilocal 2-broadcasting.

IV.2 Optimal unilocal broadcasting for two-qubit pure state

V Approximate broadcasting of a set of quantum states

V.1 Fidelity of broadcasting a set of quantum states

The no-go theorem for simultaneously broadcasting quantum states [3] says that we cannot perfectly broadcast two arbitrary noncommuting states. It is natural to ask how well we can do the task approximately. Generally, given mm states ρi\rho_{i} with respective prior probability pip_{i}, how large average fidelity can we achieve when broadcasting these states via the same channel? Mathematically, assuming the given states ρi\rho_{i} are on the system AA, we study how to optimize the nn-broadcasting fidelity gn​(η)g_{n}(\eta) of an ensemble η:={pi,ρi}i=1m\eta\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{p_{i},\rho_{i}\}_{i=1}^{m}, which is defined as

gn(η):=sup∑i=1m∑j=1n1n​pi​F​(ρi,ρ^i​j)s.t.ρ^i​j=Tr\AjΛA→A1⋯An(ρi),Λ​ is a quantum channel.\begin{split}g_{n}(\eta)\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\sup&\ \sum_{i=1}^{m}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\frac{1}{n}p_{i}F(\rho_{i},\widehat{\rho}_{ij})\\ \mathrm{s.t.}&\ \widehat{\rho}_{ij}=\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{j}}\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}\cdots A_{n}}(\rho_{i}),\\ &\ \Lambda\text{ is a quantum channel}.\end{split} (26)

Using the idea in the derivation of Eq. (10), namely, exploiting the symmetry in the broadcasting channel Λ\Lambda, we can simplify this definition. The nn-broadcasting fidelity gng_{n} of an ensemble η:={pi,ρi}i=1m\eta\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}=\{p_{i},\rho_{i}\}_{i=1}^{m} can be rewritten as

gn(η)=sup∑i=1mpi​F​(ρi,ρ^i​1)s.t.ρ^i​1=Tr\A1ΛA→A1⋯An(ρi),Λ​ is a symmetric broadcasting channel.\begin{split}g_{n}(\eta)=\sup&\ \sum_{i=1}^{m}p_{i}F(\rho_{i},\widehat{\rho}_{i1})\\ \mathrm{s.t.}&\ \widehat{\rho}_{i1}=\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{1}}\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}\cdots A_{n}}(\rho_{i}),\\ &\ \Lambda\text{ is a symmetric broadcasting channel}.\end{split} (27)
Theorem 12

The output state on system A1A_{1} of broadcasting ρi\rho_{i} is

ρ^i​1=Tr\A1ΛA→A1⋯An(ρi)=Tr\A1(JAA1⋯AnρiT),\widehat{\rho}_{i1}=\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{1}}\Lambda_{A\to A_{1}\cdots A_{n}}(\rho_{i})=\operatorname{Tr}_{\backslash A_{1}}(J_{AA_{1}\cdots A_{n}}\rho_{i}^{T}), (28)

VI Conclusions and discussion

In summary, we have studied the approximate broadcasting of quantum correlations from several aspects. Firstly, we extend the operational characterization of one-sided quantum discord to two-sided one, that is, the asymptotic optimal average mutual information loss after the action of two local broadcasting channels is equal to the two-sided quantum discord. Then we give an alternate derivation for the SDP characterization of the unilocal broadcasting fidelity, based on which we analyze some properties of unilocal broadcasting. We show that the universal quantum clone machine (UQCM) is also the optimal universal unilocal broadcasting operation. Moreover, the optimal state-dependent unilocal broadcasting operation for pure two-qubit states is analytically solved. Finally, we also formulate the broadcasting of a finite set of quantum states as an SDP. It would be of interest to study other topics related to broadcasting and correlations, such as the broadcasting of Gaussian state and correlation, and the relation between Gaussian quantum broadcasting and Gaussian quantum discord. One can also study the asymptotic behavior of the nn-broadcasting fidelity of a finite set of quantum states in the large nn limit.
